title: Redwood discovery - model selection - Deepfjord Analytics
summary: Intro discovery focused on model selection for multilingual document understanding and tool-calling. Customer weighing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for data residency and low-latency requirements. Agreed next steps include sharing security docs, pricing band, and running a short benchmark with their sample workload.
topics: tool-calling / function calling for retrieval and DB lookups
hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 + security pack (Maya)
Evan to share pricing bands for Hosted/Dedicated/Private and reserved capacity options
Deepfjord to provide sample dataset and end-to-end evaluation spec by 2027-07-02
Follow-up call to discuss pilot contract terms
action_items: Maya - send security pack and architecture note - due 2027-06-28
Evan - pricing bands + example contract summary - due 2027-06-29
Sofia - upload 3 sample documents + evaluation criteria - due 2027-07-02

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-25 16:30 PDT | Duration 52m | Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Raj (CTO, Deepfjord), Sofia (Head of ML), Liam (Infra), Priya (PM)

00:00 Raj: hey everyone uh thanks for doing this, appreciate it. we wanna run through our model selection needs and see how Redwood fits hosted vs dedicated vs private, especially around multi-lingual docs and tool calls.
00:15 Evan (AE): thanks Raj, yeah excited to chat. quick intros — im Evan AE, Maya is our solutions engineer who will do most of the deep tech, Jordan will loop in later for CSM stuff.
00:30 Maya (SE): hi all. quick agenda: current stack, scale, latency targets, security constraints, then model tradeoffs (open models, context length, quantization), and finish with next steps. sound good?
00:45 Raj: sounds great. so quick context — Deepfjord processes marine logistics docs and multilingual customs forms, about 12k docs a day, peaks up to 40k. latency target for user-facing tools is sub-300ms token latency ideally, and we have strict data residency requirements for EU customers.
01:05 Sofia: our main tasks: document extraction, Q&A over long documents (60k tokens common), and tool-calling to fetch metadata from our DB and call an automated classifier. we also need Spanish, Portuguese, and occasional Chinese support. accuracy on Spanish technical terms is critical.
01:30 Liam: infra -- we run on AWS in eu-west-1 and will need private networking for certain customers; we have strict egress rules.
01:40 Evan: perfect. quick question — when you say 60k tokens, is that per doc or per session?
01:45 Sofia: per doc. often customers upload large manifest files with appendices, so the context window matters a lot.
01:55 Maya: ok that immediately maps to model selection. options are: high-context open models (we have curated 64k and 128k variants), or you can chunk + retrieval. tradeoffs are latency and cost; larger context models often cost more and have different inference footprints.
02:15 Raj: can you clarify hosted vs dedicated vs private in that context? if we go hosted, do you support private VPC peering or is data routed through Redwood infra?
02:30 Evan: hosted is our managed API, data can stay encrypted in transit and at rest, and we have options for dedicated tenancy. for strict residency and network isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our infra with tenancy, Private is customer-deployed control plane (VPC/on-prem). both can meet your requirements but have different procurement/contract dances.
02:55 Maya: from performance side, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower noisy-neighbor variance; Private gives you full network control and avoids egress for EU-only workloads. Hosted is fastest to onboard though.
03:10 Priya: procurement note — we have one major enterprise customer who needs SOC2 Type II and SSO, and we need KMS integration for key management. typical enterprise asks, right?
03:25 Maya: absolutely. we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations. i'll include the SOC2 package in the follow-up.
03:35 Sofia: on models — we've been testing a few open models in-house. curiosity: how do Redwood-curated models compare vs upstream OpenAI or Anthropic on multilingual MRR and pragmatic factuality?
03:50 Maya: good question. we benchmark on your workload typically. general guidance: some open models with instruction tuning do better on multilingual out-of-the-box, but performance varies by domain. Redwood provides performance profiles and recommended quantization levels per model; we also do evals on your test-set to pick the best fit. many customers prefer a 64k open model variant for cost/perf balance, but if you truly need 128k or 256k windows, we can provision those as model variants.
04:20 Raj: 256k sounds huge — is that production-ready?
04:25 Maya: it's more niche; 128k is more common today for long-docs. 256k increases memory and latency significantly; you'd typically combine with retrieval and KV cache to avoid feeding the whole doc every time.
04:40 Sofia: what's KV cache? some docs we've seen reference 'KV cache' for generation speedups.
04:45 Maya: KV cache is the key-value cache of past attention states; it allows faster generation on repeated prefixes. in practice, for long doc QA we use a combination of prefix caching, retrieval, and chunked attention to keep latency acceptable. the transcriber sometimes writes it as K V cache, so that shows up in some export notes.
05:05 Liam: latency-wise, if we need sub-300ms token latency with a 64k model on Dedicated, realistic?
05:15 Maya: depends on batching and throughput. with dedicated GPUs and tuned runtime we can be under target for many workloads, but high concurrency will push us to larger clusters. we can propose batching strategies that keep P99 latency within your SLO.
05:30 Raj: how about tool-calling? we need function-calling to do retrieval + DB lookups; prefer structured responses so downstream services can ingest them.
05:45 Maya: Redwood supports tool-calling / function calling — you can define schemas. we also have built-in reranking and retrieval connectors. sometimes the transcription will show 'function call' as 'function caller' or similar, it's not perfect in exports.
06:00 Sofia: multilingual nuance — Spanish technical tokenization sometimes breaks things in models. any recommendations?
06:10 Maya: for that we usually recommend fine-tuning or instruction-tuning on domain-specific Spanish corpora, or using a model with stronger multilingual pretraining. Redwood can host your private fine-tune artifacts on Dedicated/Private. we also provide quantization recommendations — e.g., 4-bit vs 8-bit — that balance quality and cost.
06:30 Raj: talk to me about cost — hosted per-token pricing vs Dedicated reserved capacity. we have seasonal spikes.
06:40 Evan: Hosted is usage-based per token, simple to get started, good for unpredictable workloads. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits and is more cost-efficient at scale and gives you predictable throughput. Private has licensing and support fees but is best for strict compliance. Evan: i'll send a comparison spreadsheet after the call.
07:00 Priya: procurement will want to see example contract language for data residency and breach notification timelines.
07:10 Maya: noted. we'll include a template.
07:20 Raj: one more technical — can Redwood's runtime support custom kernels or custom ops? we have some optimized tokenizers and a custom embedding step we want to run as part of the pipeline.
07:35 Maya: we can add pre/post processing hooks and sometimes custom ops for Private deployments. for Hosted it's more constrained, but Dedicated can support more custom work via private connectors. we can scope a POC for that.
07:50 Sofia: also curious about evaluation — can Redwood run on our sample dataset and produce side-by-side metrics vs OpenAI?
08:00 Maya: yes, that's a standard engagement. if you share the dataset we run a benchmark and present accuracy, latency, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll include multilingual breakdowns.
08:15 Raj: timeline — we want a pilot in Q3. procurement & legal need to sign off. roadmap wise, we'd like a 6-8 week pilot including benchmarking and an initial deployment.
08:30 Evan: sounds reasonable. next steps: Maya sends security pack; I send pricing and pilot contract outline; Sofia uploads samples; then schedule the benchmarking session.
08:45 Priya: can you also include an estimate for reserved capacity vs burst capacity? we sometimes need burst during reporting windows.
08:55 Maya: yes, we'll show autoscaling & burst options, and how we handle fallback to smaller models if capacity constrained.
09:10 Raj: any immediate concerns from you — either Redwood about our constraints or us about onboarding?
09:20 Maya: only that we need the samples and network diagram (Liam) to size pods and pick Dedicated vs Private. also confirm which EU regions you must keep data in.
09:35 Liam: we'll send the VPC diagram and EU-only list.
09:40 Sofia: one last thing — tool-calling latency must be low; DB lookups should not add more than 100ms. is that achievable?
09:50 Maya: yes with local caching and colocated infra it's feasible; we'll lay out the recommended architecture in the follow-up doc.
10:05 Evan: ok recapping next steps and owners. thanks everyone — we'll follow up early next week.
10:15 Raj: thanks, talk soon.

Notes: transcription has minor speaker attribution glitches and a few OCR-like substitutions (e.g., 'K V cache', 'quant' for quantization); recorded duration 52m. Links mentioned: security pack (link in follow-up), benchmark template: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks-template (placeholder).
